Implementation Plan

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends _rb_fix_scope_is_protected
Scope-mode justification: The finding is narrow. Inside `rb_fix_scope_check` in `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh`, the `ALLOW_WORKFLOW_EDITS=false` rejection list is `scripts/*|prompts/*|.github/ai/*|.github/workflows/*`. The protected-path helper `_rb_fix_scope_is_protected`, defined a few lines earlier, already covers `.github/actions/*` and `.claude/*`. So the two lists have drifted apart, and neither one covers `workflow-templates/*`. The complete fix is about 10 lines: one shared path predicate that covers `workflow-templates/*` and is used by both checks, plus tests and docs. This is within the Boil the Lake bound and adds no new dependency or interface. Per §6, Security > Correctness & safety > Backward compatibility > Operational clarity > Performance > Speed, and closing the whole drift (not just the cited paths) is the correctness win. The `forbidden_artifact`, `workflow_edits_disabled`, `protected_not_in_pr` and `out_of_scope` reason tokens and all log prefixes stay the same. I did not widen the set to all of `.github/*`, because `CODEOWNERS` and `dependabot.yml` are not executable automation and the finding does not ask for them (see D2).

Planning ref: `git rev-parse HEAD` = `6a93f5d8dad2fc20f6956627ebc4363210c3c8d9`, branch `claude/lucid-ptolemy-f20vwu`, which matches the integration branch metadata (mismatch: false). Dependency #6389 is CLOSED with `ai:merged`; its PR-files-only scope check is on this ref (the `# Refs #6389` comment in `rb_fix_scope_check`).

Automation / §20.E:
- No new script. This changes only existing code in `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh`, inside the review-blocked fix path.
- No new scheduler wiring. The code already runs on every poll tick from `.github/workflows/orchestrate_poll.yml`, called by `.github/workflows/internal-orchestrate-poll.yml` (cron `*/5 * * * *`) and the consumer `workflow-templates/ai-orchestrate-poll.yml`.
- No new long-running supervisor.
- No database work.
- No `docs/scripts-pending-removal.md` entry, because no script is added.

1. Files likely to change
- `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh`: the review-blocked fix block, which defines `_rb_fix_scope_is_protected` and `rb_fix_scope_check`.
- `tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py`: new tests next to `test_review_blocked_fix_scope_rejects_workflow_edit_opt_out`, using the existing `_review_blocked_fix_scope_case` helper.
- `agents.md`: the "Isolated Codex agents" → "Trusted copies" bullet that reads "When `ALLOW_WORKFLOW_EDITS=false`, staged edits to `scripts/`, `prompts/`, `.github/ai/`, or `.github/workflows/` reject through that same path…".
- `changelog.d/6390-review-blocked-workflow-opt-out-paths.md` (new; `<!-- changelog: security -->` fragment, same format as `changelog.d/6389-review-blocked-fix-scope-pr-files-only.md`).

2. Functions or modules to implement
- `_rb_fix_scope_is_protected()` (existing; extend it, do not rename). The case list becomes:
  `.github/workflows/*|.github/actions/*|.github/ai/*|scripts/*|prompts/*|.claude/*|workflow-templates/*) return 0 ;;`
  Add a comment saying this one predicate is both the protected-path set and the `ALLOW_WORKFLOW_EDITS` opt-out set (Refs #6390), so the two cannot drift again. Give each entry a one-line rationale: `workflow-templates/*` is synced into consumer repos as workflows and `.claude/` hooks; `.github/actions/*` holds composite actions that workflows execute; `.claude/*` holds hooks and settings Claude Code executes.
- `rb_fix_scope_check()`: in the first staged-path loop, keep `.github/prompts/*|.github/scripts/*` → `forbidden_artifact` exactly as it is, and evaluate it first. Replace the hard-coded `scripts/*|prompts/*|.github/ai/*|.github/workflows/*)` arm with a default arm:
  ```
  *)
    if [ "${ALLOW_WORKFLOW_EDITS:-true}" != "true" ] && _rb_fix_scope_is_protected "${path}"; then
      [ "${RB_FIX_SCOPE_REASON}" = forbidden_artifact ] || RB_FIX_SCOPE_REASON=workflow_edits_disabled
      RB_FIX_SCOPE_REJECTED_PATHS+=("${path}")
    fi ;;
  ```
  Everything else stays as it is: the reason precedence, reporting every rejected path (comma list in `REVIEW_BLOCKED_FIX_SCOPE_REJECTED`), the PR-files check, and the `protected_not_in_pr` / `out_of_scope` classification. Because the PR-files stage also calls `_rb_fix_scope_is_protected`, a `workflow-templates/*` path outside the PR now reports `protected_not_in_pr` instead of `out_of_scope`. It was rejected before as well; only the reason token changes.
- Do not change the staging pathspec (`git add -A -- . ':!.github/prompts' ':!.github/scripts'`). Staging stays broad on purpose so excluded edits cannot hide behind an allowed fix, as the existing comment says.

3. Data structures affected
- None persisted. The `RB_FIX_SCOPE_REASON` / `RB_FIX_SCOPE_REJECTED_PATHS` shell variables keep their meaning. The retry-state increment (`review_blocked_retries`) on a rejection is unchanged.

4. API or interface changes
- No new env vars, log prefixes, labels or GitHub API calls (§14: no new `gh` calls; the existing paginated `pulls/<n>/files` listing is untouched).
- Behaviour change, operator-visible: when `ALLOW_WORKFLOW_EDITS=false`, review-blocked fixes that touch `workflow-templates/**`, `.github/actions/**` or `.claude/**` are now rejected with `reason=workflow_edits_disabled`, even when the PR itself changed those files. With the default `ALLOW_WORKFLOW_EDITS=true`, nothing changes for files in the PR.

## Decisions
### D1 — One shared predicate for the protected set and the opt-out set
- Chosen: route the `ALLOW_WORKFLOW_EDITS` opt-out check through the existing `_rb_fix_scope_is_protected` and add `workflow-templates/*` to it.
- Alternatives considered: append `workflow-templates/*|.github/actions/*|.claude/*` to the inline opt-out case arm only; add a second, separate helper.
- Why: the bypass exists because two hard-coded lists drifted apart. A single predicate removes that class of bug, and it reuses an existing helper instead of adding a new identifier (§10).

### D2 — Keep the set at executable automation assets, not all of `.github/*`
- Chosen: `.github/workflows/`, `.github/actions/`, `.github/ai/`, `scripts/`, `prompts/`, `.claude/`, `workflow-templates/`.
- Alternatives considered: reuse the integration-judge `PROTECTED_PATH_GLOBS` set (`.github/*|…|validation/*|ai-memory/*|db/contracts/*` plus build/config basenames); block all of `.github/*`.
- Why: `ALLOW_WORKFLOW_EDITS` is documented as a workflow-automation opt-out. The judge set guards conflict-merge provenance in an unrelated way, and applying it here would block legitimate consumer fixes to `*.json`/`*.yml`/build files that the PR itself changed. That would go beyond the finding (§9). Out-of-PR edits to any path are already rejected by the #6389 PR-files gate.

### D3 — Keep the reason tokens
- Chosen: reuse `workflow_edits_disabled` and `protected_not_in_pr`.
- Alternatives considered: a new reason such as `template_edits_disabled`.
- Why: log tokens are contractual for log analysis (§10), and the existing token already describes the condition.

## Security considerations
- Trust boundary: the judge's working tree, written by a prompt-injectable model running in the isolated container, crosses into a `GH_TOKEN`-authenticated `git push` made by the poller. `rb_fix_scope_check` is the last deterministic gate before commit and push.
- Authorization: the repo-level `ALLOW_WORKFLOW_EDITS=false` opt-out must apply to every path that becomes executable automation: in this repo (`.github/actions`, `.claude/hooks`), or in every consumer repo through the `@stable` sync (`workflow-templates/**`, which includes `workflow-templates/.claude/**`).
- Input validation: paths come from `git diff --cached --name-only --no-renames -z`, which is NUL-safe. Case matching is literal; GitHub only runs `.github/workflows` and `.github/actions` at their exact-case paths, so a case-variant path is not executable there and is still bound by the PR-files gate.
- Abuse cases covered:
  - (a) An injected judge edits `workflow-templates/ai-review.yml`, which this PR also changed, while the opt-out is set → rejected.
  - (b) It edits `.github/actions/<x>/action.yml` → rejected.
  - (c) It edits `.claude/hooks/gh_api_write_guard.py` to weaken the permission guard → rejected.
  - (d) It mixes an allowed `sandbox_fix.txt` edit with one of these → the whole fix is rejected (no partial commit), as today.
  - (e) A rename such as `workflow-templates/a.yml` → `src/a.yml`: `--no-renames` lists the deletion side, so it is caught.
- Fails closed: a rejection consumes one retry, sends the WARNING Telegram and does not push. That is unchanged.
- No money state, secrets or logging of sensitive values are involved.

Failure modes:
- Trigger: a consumer with `ALLOW_WORKFLOW_EDITS=false` has a review-blocked PR whose real fix is in `workflow-templates/` or `.claude/`. Symptom: `REVIEW_BLOCKED_FIX_SCOPE_REJECTED … reason=workflow_edits_disabled`, plus a WARNING. Recovery: the existing retry budget, then `close_and_reissue` or human handling. This is the intended opt-out semantics.
- Trigger: a bash `case` typo. Symptom: the tests below fail in CI. Recovery: fix before merge.

5. Potential risks or edge cases
- Conflict detection: the issue says "the rejection list omits workflow-templates/ and .github/actions/". The code confirms it, and also shows `.claude/` is missing from the opt-out list even though `_rb_fix_scope_is_protected` contains it. The fix covers all three.
